title: Text you type on a screen does not wear the screenshot halo
goal: Words typed on a screenshot get a soft white glow behind them so they stay readable over a photo. A label typed straight onto a screen you are designing does not need it, and there it reads as a smudge. Text inside a screen should be drawn clean, the same way text inside a component now is.
notes: Follow-on from the component halo task (2026-09-03). The rule is already built: Layer.drawnShadow(insideComponent:) plus an insideComponent flag threaded through DocumentRenderer.compositeLayers/groupImage. Widening it means deciding whether a frame counts the same way a component does, and whether a plain group nested inside a frame counts. A frame is group.isFrame with a backgroundHex, so the predicate is one clause; the question is a UX one, because a caption deliberately laid over a screenshot placed inside a frame would lose its halo too. Consider whether the trigger should be the frame having a painted surface rather than being a frame at all.
acceptance: A text layer inside a frame draws with no halo
Text on the open canvas still keeps its halo over a screenshot
Putting existing text into a frame drops the halo, and taking it out puts it back
A before and after picture is in the audit
